context:
Fix the cheap, proven cause first and re-measure before touching anything else -- the three workflows may not share a root cause.

DECISION GATE w3: after the 3.10 and Windows causes are addressed, decide per still-red workflow whether it is (a) a real product defect to fix, (b) a genuinely environment-specific test to gate to the platforms it supports, or (c) a check to retire. Record the choice and reason. A perma-red required-adjacent workflow is not an acceptable steady state; neither is silencing a check that is catching a real defect.
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-23. Three develop workflows have failed every scheduled run for at least five days:
 - Nightly Validation: failure on 2026-08-19/20/21/22/23
 - Release Canary: failure 2026-08-22 and 2026-08-23, cancelled 08-19 through 08-21
 - Corpus Drift Check: failure on 2026-08-19 through 2026-08-23

One root cause is identified and is a one-line fix. tests/uat/clickhouse_memory.py:309 calls _dt.datetime.now(_dt.UTC). datetime.UTC is Python 3.11+, and the project declares Python 3.10+ support (README, pyproject requires-python). Every test in tests/uat/test_clickhouse_memory.py fails on ubuntu-latest/3.10 with AttributeError: module 'datetime' has no attribute 'UTC'. This is TEST-ONLY: grep for datetime.UTC across benchbox/ returns zero hits, so the shipped package is not affected on 3.10 -- but the gate stays red.

Windows 3.10/3.12 also fail, on a different cause: benchbox.mcp.jobs durable jobs do not reach 'completed' (tests/... assert job state 'queued'/'failed' != 'completed', ExceptionGroup at benchbox/mcp/jobs.py:771). Release Canary fails in 'credential-free non-fast canary (shard 4/6)'. These are separate root causes and must not be assumed fixed by the 3.10 fix.

Why this is customer-facing rather than process hygiene: docs/operations/release-guide.md:80-88 requires committed UAT evidence at _project/release-evidence/uat-gate-summary.json with a green verdict, at most 21 days old, or validate-base fails the release PR. That directory contains only README.md today. cut-v0-4-0-release therefore cannot proceed, and v0.4.0 is how benchbox.dev/results/ and 45 days of product work reach users.

anti_patterns.dont: Assume one root cause fixes all three workflows
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD confirm each independently in w0
anti_patterns.why: the 3.10, Windows-MCP and canary-shard failures are demonstrably different

anti_patterns.dont: Bump the project's Python floor to 3.11 to make the nightly pass
anti_patterns.why: it drops supported users to avoid a one-line test fix

anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD produce it from a real green sweep
anti_patterns.why: the gate exists to prove a sweep actually ran

anti_patterns.dont: Mark the failing jobs continue-on-error or remove them from the schedule
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD apply the w3 decision with a recorded reason
anti_patterns.why: the release gate then reports green on unverified ground

anti_patterns.dont: treat a green make pr-preflight as covering integration tests
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD when a change edits user-visible CLI text, grep tests/integration and tests/e2e for the old string before opening the PR
anti_patterns.why: pr-preflight runs the fast lane only, so PR #1844's docstring edit passed preflight and broke Release Canary shard 4/6 on tests/integration/test_platforms_cli_integration.py

anti_patterns.dont: write a version-floor guard that checks only the one construct you just saw
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD cover the whole class (attributes AND stdlib module imports), and verify on the real floor with 'uv run --python 3.10' rather than reasoning about it
anti_patterns.why: the #1838 guard checked ATTRIBUTE ACCESS only (datetime.UTC) and missed a bare 'import tomllib' three days later, taking ubuntu-latest/3.10 red again

preserves.behavior: No check is retired merely because it is red; retirement requires the w3 decision and a recorded reason
Python 3.10 stays supported for as long as pyproject requires-python says so; the fix is to the test, not to the support floor

work_units.evidence: Fixed in PR #1838: _dt.timezone.utc, plus tests/unit/test_python_version_floor_guard.py (AST-based, reads floor from pyproject, negative control proves it fires on the original line). make pr-preflight green: 28,010 passed.

DIAGNOSED 2026-08-23 from run 32622645993 (Nightly) and 32628137865 (Release Canary). These are NOT one cause.

RELEASE CANARY shard 4/6: a single hanging test, not a timeout-config problem. Other shards finish in 13-21 min; shard 4 ran 53 min and was killed with exit 143. The log's last line is 'tests/uat/test_cli_dispatch.py' at 08:38:40 with no dot before the 09:18 kill. The only non-fast test in that module is test_completeness_gate_digest_provenance. Its comment says 'Using 0-scale tpch with local-only platform keeps the sweep cheap', but validate_config({'name':..., 'phases':[...]}) leaves platforms.include=() with include_was_specified=False, so no filter applies and orchestrator.run_sweep runs the FULL platform matrix at SF0.01 with no time bound. Reproduced locally: the test ran over 27 minutes before I killed it. Fix is small -- pin platforms.include and benchmarks.include to what the comment already claims.

NIGHTLY: 5 failing jobs, at least 5 distinct causes. 'test (ubuntu-latest, 3.10)' is the datetime.UTC break already fixed in PR #1838. The Windows failures (3.10, 3.12, plus integration-smoke 3.12) are ~24 tests in at least five groups: (1) MCP durable jobs never reach 'completed' (7 tests, jobs stay queued/failed, plus one rate-limit ExceptionGroup) -- the only genuinely product-facing group; (2) worktree make targets, 11 tests, all failing on shell/awk/make assumptions that do not hold on Windows ('awk: escape sequence \\U', 'fatal: could not create leading directories'); (3) POSIX path assumptions ('\\tmp\\db.duckdb' == '/tmp/db.duckdb', makefile inventory symlink resolution); (4) signal.SIGKILL, which does not exist on Windows; (5) a pytest-benchmark/xdist warning surfacing as a failure. Groups 2, 3 and 5 are agent-tooling tests, not shipped-product tests. 'scheduled-workflow-liveness' is a separate job and untriaged.

Feeds w3: my recommendation is to scope groups 2/3/5 to POSIX (they gate make targets that only ever run on the maintainer machine and Linux CI, and no Windows support is claimed for them), fix the shard 4 hang, and treat the MCP durable-jobs group as the one real Windows product question.
work_units.summary: Diagnose the Windows durable-MCP-job failure and the Release Canary shard 4/6 failure as separate causes

work_units.evidence:
DECISION recorded, PR #1853. Four of the five Windows failure groups handled, and two turned out to be real test defects rather than platform limits, so they are FIXED rather than skipped -- better than the fix/scope/retire framing assumed.

FIXED, coverage kept: (1) test_a_path_object_is_stringified asserted the literal '/tmp/db.duckdb'; the property under test is 'a Path becomes a str', not the host separator, and str(Path('/tmp/db.duckdb')) is '\\tmp\\db.duckdb' on Windows with the behaviour correct -- now compares against str(database_path). (2) test_timeout_path_drains_using_the_reap_timeout_constant patched os.killpg with raising=False but not the signals; the ladder evaluates signal.SIGKILL as an ARGUMENT to os.killpg, so Windows raised AttributeError before the call. Injecting both signals is the technique the two sibling tests in that module already use, and their comments say explicitly that a skipif would drop the POSIX branch under test.

SCOPED TO POSIX: tests/integration/worktree/test_worktree_release_dirty_guard.py (module) -- it drives make worktree-create/remove, maintainer and agent tooling with no claimed Windows support, failing in the tooling (awk escape sequences, could not create leading directories) rather than the behaviour, 11 of 18 red. This also drops the 7 that currently pass; recorded as an explicit trade, not hidden. And test_absolute_symlink_makefile_preserves_module_resolution, since creating a symlink on Windows needs elevation.

NOT TOUCHED, deliberately: the MCP durable-jobs group (7 tests, jobs never reaching 'completed') is the one genuinely product-facing Windows question and needs a decision, not a skip. A NoneType.splitlines() in the makefile inventory guard and a pytest-benchmark/xdist warning surfacing as a failure in the release curation guard are not honestly diagnosable from a log without a Windows machine; guessing is how a skip lands on a test that would have passed.

work_units.evidence:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED IN PRODUCTION, 2026-08-23T20:12. PR #1847 fixes it.

Original diagnosis: the mirror to published-results last succeeded 2026-08-06; PR #1614 (2026-08-05 client_host strip) rewrote bundle bytes without rerunning _project/scripts/results_explorer_corpus_migrate.py, leaving 105 sidecar bundle_hash values stale, and the mirror's own validation refuses to open on a hash mismatch.

Independent confirmation later the same day: merging #1843 to develop touched results-data/ -- the first push to that path since 2026-08-05 -- which fired the mirror's push trigger. Run 32663701598 opened mirror PR #1851 and posted commit status corpus-mirror/validate-bundles = FAILURE with exactly 105 'Bundle hash mismatch' errors, the same 105. So the mirror was never disabled or misconfigured; it simply had no trigger for 17 days, and the moment it got one it failed for precisely the recorded reason.

CORRECTION to the earlier wording: 'the mirror has not run since 2026-08-06' was accurate when written but is now superseded -- it ran on 2026-08-23 and failed.

CONSEQUENCE: mirror PR #1851 currently carries the stale hashes and a failing validation status. It must be regenerated after #1847 merges (gh workflow run sync-results-data-to-published.yml --ref develop) rather than merged as it stands.

Fix in #1847: rerun the migration tool -- 105 manifests, one line each, plus a migration ledger; changed_bundles=0, so develop's bundle bytes were already correct and only the recorded hashes were stale. scripts/validate_submission.py --allow-partial-validation now 207/207 PASS exit 0. Guard added to the whole-corpus lane with two synthetic negative controls.
